lenses.reason: Forced CA parsing, certutil initialization, cert import, Chrome spawn, and pre-CDP startup failures through their callers.

lenses.reason: Traced caCert through CLI, config, schemas, MCP, daemon env, launch commands, hashes, fingerprints, and Eve.

lenses.name: Boundary pipeline trace

lenses.reason: Compared help, README, schemas, web docs, skill docs, and Eve documentation with the driven behavior and rejection set.

lenses.name: Complexity budget
lenses.reason: CA import is linear in bundle certificate count and occurs once per Chromium launch.

findings.claim: A certutil preparation failure leaked the temporary Chromium profile.
findings.evidence: Forced missing and failing certutil paths left a profile before the fix; try_launch_chrome now removes temp_user_data_dir when prepare_nss_home fails, and the Linux matrix observes no profile increase.

findings.claim: Local state commands incorrectly loaded and validated browser CA configuration.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, --ca-cert /missing state list failed before the local state dispatch; validation now occurs after dispatch_state_command and the command succeeds.
findings.path: main -> dispatch_state_command -> incompatible launch and CA validation

findings.claim: The new flag was absent from required commands and proxy documentation.
findings.evidence: The deterministic surface and new-flag sweeps identified the omissions; both pages now describe the Linux Chromium scope and limitations.
findings.path: ca_bundle and CLI flag -> commands/proxy docs

findings.claim: The core skill option list and Eve proxy configuration did not propagate caCert.
findings.evidence: flagsweep found the skill omission, and Eve exposed proxy without the matching CA path. The skill, Eve schema, argument translation, README, and tests now cover it.

findings.claim: Chrome startup failures before DevTools publication could delete the private NSS HOME without killing and reaping the whole Chrome process group.
findings.evidence: The error branches called child.kill without the process-group kill and wait used by ChromeProcess. terminate_launched_chrome now kills the group, waits, then cleanup removes the directories; focused tests compile and the full Linux matrix remains green.

exemptions.claim: Historical changelog entries need not mention --ca-cert.
exemptions.evidence: They describe prior releases and are not current option inventories.

exemptions.claim: The CDP mode page need not advertise --ca-cert.
exemptions.evidence: The implementation rejects CA trust with CDP attach because it cannot modify an already-running browser's NSS environment.

exemptions.claim: The chrome.rs proxy hit is not a missing public flag surface.
exemptions.evidence: It is Chromium's internal --proxy-bypass-list argument construction.
They name the Debian system package, not the --ca-cert option.

issue_candidates.title: Parallel Rust test environment interference
issue_candidates.evidence: One parallel suite run failed a restore-state unit test; the test passed isolated and the entire serial suite passed.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: The failing test and state logic are unchanged by the CA diff and indicate a pre-existing environment-mutating test race.

issue_candidates.title: SIGKILL leaves an NSS HOME orphan
issue_candidates.evidence: The Linux matrix observes one additional private NSS directory after killing the daemon with SIGKILL.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: No destructor can run after SIGKILL, and PID-based sweeping could delete a live concurrent session after PID reuse.
